Brokerage accounts typically offer the following types of sell orders:

1. Market Order 
A market order is the simplest type of sell order. A market order instructs the broker to sell the stock at the current market price, which means the price may vary widely depending on market conditions. Since a market order doesn't specify a price, it ensures a quick sell at whatever price is available at that moment. However, the uncertainty surrounding the price can cause the investor to risk selling their stock at a lower price than they would want it to. 2. Limit Order 
A limit order sets a specific price that an investor wants to sell their stock at. When placing a limit sell order, the broker will only execute the trade if the stock price reaches the specified limit price. This is useful when an investor wants to sell the stock at a specific price or higher. An advantage of a limit order is that the investor can have control over the price at which the stock is sold. 3. Stop-Loss Order 
A stop-loss order instructs a broker to sell a stock once it reaches a specific price. The stop-loss order is designed to mitigate losses in case the stock price falls to a predetermined level, often set up as a percentage of the purchase price. This sell order is beneficial because the investor can minimize potential losses or avoid further losses if the stock trend goes south. 4. Stop-Limit Order 
A stop-limit order is a combination of a limit order and a stop-loss order. Specifically, the stop limit sell order becomes active when the stock reaches the stop price and continues to work as a limit order where the broker will sell at the specified limit price. This type of sell order can be particularly useful when an investor is hoping to maximize profits while minimizing risk. In conclusion, these are typically the different sell orders available for an investor in a brokerage account. - The price at which the stock is sold is under control of the investor.

Disadvantages:
- The price may not be reached for sale due to market fluctuations, leading to a missed selling opportunity.

The Fashion Girl’s Guide To Washington, D.C.
Many will flock to the nation’s capital next weekend for the presidential inauguration and the Women’s March on Washington, which is set to take place the day after the official festivities. It’s been a while since we’ve thought about D.C. In terms of must-visit destinations—it’s so difficult to focus on any one city, with all of these places to see—but it’s absolutely a place worth adding to your bucket list for 2017. Here, our guide on where to stay, what to eat and how to shop (and more!) when you’re in the nation’s capital.
If you're going to D.C. For the inauguration or for the March, we hope you've already booked your lodging, since the prices for everything from the Holiday Inn to a stranger's couch are beyond exorbitant at this point. On a normal weekend, however, we love the infamous Watergate Hotel, of which the Nixonian scandal received its moniker. The hotel closed in 2007, but just re-opened last summer after a $125 million renovation. The revamp includes charming details, like employee uniforms by Mad Men costume designer Jamie Bryant and pens labeled "Stolen from the Watergate Hotel." All of this makes for retro-yet-luxurious vibes that set the perfect stage for enjoying a midday cocktail without judgment.
Our top pick for dining in D.C. Is Bad Saint, which Bon Appetit named the second-best restaurant in America in 2016. ( The New York Times seconded the recommendation just two months ago.) The Filipino restaurant doesn't take reservations, so wait times can be long—here are some tips for getting in.
Other options include: Rasika, known as one of the best Indian restaurants in the country; Rose's Luxury, also a Bon Appetit best-restaurant winner; Blue Duck Tavern, where POTUS and FLOTUS celebrated their anniversary in 2009; Hazel or Maketto for dim sum brunch; Fiola Mare, home to President Obama's 55th birthday celebration; The Red Hen for D.C.'s best Italian; Little Serow, for an affordable prix fixe menu of super-spicy Thai; and Daikaya, for a taste of D.C.'s robust ramen scene.
Tours of the Capitol are free (you can book them here), and we highly recommend you squeeze one in if this is your first time in D.C. The Smithsonian museums are great, and also free (check out the National Museum of the American Indian, it's a favorite), but we definitely suggest prioritizing a visit to the Phillips Collection instead if you're short on time. For something a little less educational, try the 9:30 Club, an iconic music venue where surprise performers often include mega-stars like Radiohead. You should also check out the programming at The Kennedy Center while you're in town, as the building itself is something to behold. And no trip to D.C. Is complete without some time spent at the National Mall, a two-mile stretch of greenery that's also home to some of the nation's most prominent monuments.
To give your wardrobe a D.C.-enabled makeover, make sure to hit up these independent shops: Violet in Georgetown for affordable and on-trend clothes and accessories; Secondi in Dupont for second-hand designer workwear; Redeem for hard-to-find lines like GHSTS and Kowtow; Lynn Louisa for Rachel Comey, Line and other faves; Meeps/Treasury in Adams Morgan for vintage finds; and Relish, for classically tailored pieces.
For home goods, don't miss Miss Pixie's and Salt & Sundry on 14th Street; Salt & Sundry's new sister shop, Little Leaf; and The Eastern Market flea on Saturdays and Sundays, near Capitol Hill.
Book lovers should check out Politics & Prose, which also offers some amazing author events, as well as Capitol Hill Books and Kramerbooks.

Ingredients:
- 1 pie crust (store-bought or homemade)
- 2-3 large apples, peeled and sliced
- 3 tbsp sugar
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 1 tbsp flour
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp butter, cut into small pieces
- 1 egg, lightly beaten for egg wash
- Coarse sugar, for sprinkling

Directions:
1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. Roll out the pie crust on a floured surface and cut into 4-6 circles. Place the circles onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
3. In a medium bowl, mix together the sugar, cinnamon, and flour. Add in the sliced apples and lemon juice, stirring until the apples are coated.
4. Spoon the apple mixture onto the center of each pie crust, leaving a border around the edges.
5. Dot the tops of the apple mixture with the butter pieces.
6. Fold up the edges of the pie crust over the apples, crimping the edges as you go.
7. Brush the edges of the pie crust with the egg wash and sprinkle with coarse sugar.
8. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the apples are tender.
9. Allow the tarts to cool for a few minutes before serving.

Passage: Starting high school can seem momentous for anyone, but banjoist Noam Pikelny's inaugural day at Niles North in Skokie, 11 years ago this week, was doubly memorable -- his picture, in color no less, was in the paper.
"My freshman year," recalls Pikelny, "on my first day, that review [of his band, Minor Bluegrass,] was on the front page of the Arts section of the Tribune. I was walking around the halls that day expecting people to notice me or something -- everyone would have seen this article! Of course, not even the teachers had seen it. But eventually, people kind of got into the fact that I played banjo."
People who are into that fact today include vocalist/bassist John Cowan -- who knows about banjo players, having played with Bela Fleck in the 1980s edition of the New Grass Revival -- and mandolin superstar Chris Thile of Nickel Creek.
Pikelny has been in the John Cowan Band for the last year and for their exceptional disc, "New Tattoo" (Pinecastle), but will be leaving soon, in part to dedicate more time to projects with Thile.
"He wants to join what I refer to as the Legion of Acoustic Superheroes," Cowan says. "Noam has more integrity than anyone I've met his age. I hate it that he's going to leave, but I kinda knew when I got him, not unlike Bela, how long could I hold on to him?"
Thile's fifth solo album, "How to Grow a Woman From the Ground" (Sugar Hill, out Sept. 12), features the band Thile formed specifically for this project -- young virtuosi who, led by Thile's mandolin and vocals, encompass the classic bluegrass quintet: Pikelny, fiddler Gabe Witcher, guitarist Chris Eldridge and bassist Greg Garrison.
Cuts such as their cover of The Strokes' "Heart in a Cage," packing more raw power than the original despite the absence of drums or amps, make "How to Grow" state-of-the-art newgrass music. Much of that track's success rests on Pikelny's recurring banjo lick.
"I get this feeling from Noam that I envy," Thile says, "that ultimately, there is really nothing that Noam can't do. ... There's a diligence that I find to be utterly remarkable. A lot of times, that diligence comes in the absence of talent -- people that are that diligent because they have to be, where Noam is one of those very rare musicians that is that diligent in addition to being ludicrously talented."
"He's doing this thing that Bela used to do," says Cowan about Pikelny, "which is, he's playing his banjo from the time he gets up 'til the time he goes to bed, just non-stop."
If Pikelny, who grew up in Skokie, tires of the inevitable comparisons to Fleck, he doesn't show it. Having studied the pre-bluegrass, clawhammer banjo as a youngster at the Old Town School of Folk Music and at Evanston's Hogeye, it was hearing Fleck and his Flecktones at Navy Pier in the early 1990s that started Pikelny on the path that is now leading him into uncharted territory. He also was lucky to discover that Greg Cahill, the founder and leader of Special Consensus, for decades the Chicago area's premier national bluegrass act, lived mere blocks away, especially fortunate for a kid not yet old enough to drive.
Cahill's influence "was immeasurable in my progression as a musician," says Pikelny about his former teacher. "I really enjoy finding a way to play something on the banjo that hasn't been played before, or an arrangement that hasn't been played before, and I think Greg was the guy who sparked that for me."
After early local experience with Lora Hebert and the Hoosier Prairie Band, with his dad driving each week to and from Valparaiso, Ind., and Minor Bluegrass, which included fiddler Casey Driessen, another musician whose star is in ascent, Pikelny headed Downstate to the University of Illinois to study computer engineering. He found time for the band of composer and guitarist Slavek Hanzlik, including five weeks in the summer of 2002 touring the Czech Republic. Immediately thereafter, the musical connections Pikelny had forged in Urbana-Champaign led to an offer to replace the late Mark Van in the jam band juggernaut, Leftover Salmon.
"Going from playing at a local college bar to playing the sold out House of Blues in Chicago, or the Fillmore in Denver, it was very exhilarating and kind of scary at first," says Pikelny, who sites Leftover Salmon leader Vince Herman as a major influence, particularly on the less tangible aspects of being a musician.
"I just worshipped New Grass Revival," says Pikelny of the band that boasted, besides Cowan and Fleck, Sam Bush and Pat Flynn, and to his eternal regret, broke up before Pikelny heard them live. "I had put them up there on a pedestal."
"[Playing in the John Cowan Band] was different than playing with Leftover Salmon," Pikelny says. "It was really my first time playing in a real bluegrass ensemble ... With guys who are master bluegrass musicians. I think playing music with Cowan has gotten me to the stage where my playing appealed to [Thile] and he wanted me to play on his record."
Though they'd jammed a bit in the past, Thile says, "There is no experience from the last several years that transcends that moment last summer at [the] Telluride [festival] where I remet Noam."
Stepping on stage for an after-hours jam, Thile spotted Pikelny.
"We started playing," Thile says, "and every note that Noam played was something I'd wished I'd played. Provide a step-by-step tutorial with measurements and ingredients clarification detailing how to make delicious hummus without the use of a food processor.Ingredients:
- 1 can of chickpeas (15 ounce)
- 2 garlic cloves
- 2 tbsp tahini
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1/2 tsp ground cumin
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/4 tsp paprika
- 1-2 tbsp lemon juice
- Water

Instructions:

1. Drain the can of chickpeas and rinse them under cold water. 

2. Mince the garlic cloves and set aside. 

3. In a pestle and mortar, grind the chickpeas until they break up and form small chunks. This may take a bit of time and effort but it worth it! 

4. Once the chickpeas are ground, add the minced garlic and grind together to combine. 

5. To make the hummus creamier, add 1-2 tablespoons of tahini paste to the pestle and mortar, and grind the mixture together. 

6. Once the tahini has been mixed into the mixture, add 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon of ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon of paprika to the bowl. 

7. Use a spoon to mix everything together until it forms a paste.

8. Add a splash of fresh lemon juice to the hummus to brighten its flavor. 

9. Gradually add water to the paste and stir until it reaches the desired consistency. 

10. Taste the hummus and adjust seasoning as necessary, adding more salt, lemon juice, or paprika to your taste. 

11. If you prefer your hummus warm, mix into simmering water and stir for a minute before serving. 

12. Decant the hummus into a serving dish, sprinkle with paprika, and drizzle some olive oil over the surface of the hummus. 

13. Serve with veggies, pita bread, or as a spread on a sandwich. 

Enjoy your delicious homemade hummus!This tutorial seems pretty straightforward, but could you give me some tips on how to make the hummus extra creamy?Sure, here are a few tips to make your hummus extra creamy:

1. Soak chickpeas overnight: Soaking the chickpeas in water overnight can make them softer and creamier. This step requires some extra time and effort, but it's worth it if you want extra creamy hummus.

2. Remove chickpeas' skins: Removing the skins of the chickpeas can make the hummus creamier. You can do this by rubbing the chickpeas between your fingers and then rinsing them under water. This step is also a bit time-consuming, but it makes the hummus ultra-smooth.

3. Use a high-speed blender: If you have a high-speed blender like a Vitamix or a Nutribullet, you can use it to blend the hummus until it's incredibly creamy. If you don't have a blender, use a food processor or a hand mixer with whisk attachments.

4. Add extra tahini: Tahini is a paste made from sesame seeds and is one of the key ingredients in hummus. Adding a bit more tahini can make the hummus creamier and richer.

5. Add more olive oil: Olive oil adds flavor and creaminess to hummus. You can add a bit more olive oil to your hummus to make it smoother and richer.

Try these tips to make your hummus extra creamy and velvety-smooth!Can you also suggest some creative ways to flavor the hummus? I love trying out new variations!Absolutely! Here are a few creative ways to flavor your hummus:

1. Roasted garlic hummus: Roasting garlic cloves can give the hummus a sweet, caramelized flavor. Can you explain the difference between a naval cruiser and a battleship?Yes! 

A naval cruiser is a type of warship that is typically smaller and faster than a battleship. Cruisers typically have a primary armament of guns, but they are usually not as large or powerful as the guns on a battleship. Cruisers are also often more heavily armed with secondary weapons, like torpedoes or anti-aircraft guns. They were typically designed for a variety of roles, including scouting, escorting other ships, and engaging enemy cruisers.

On the other hand, a battleship is a larger and more heavily armed warship that is designed for engaging other battleships. Battleships typically have much larger and more powerful guns than cruisers, and they are built with thick armor plating to withstand enemy fire. Battleships were often tasked with the role of protecting a navy's most valuable assets, such as aircraft carriers or troop transport ships, and were used primarily in major sea battles.Well, can a battleship be used for escorting other ships too or is it only for major sea battles?Yes, battleships can be used for escorting other ships as well. Battleships were often used to escort other ships such as troop transports and aircraft carriers, and were also used to provide fire support for troops onshore during amphibious assaults. However, battleships were primarily designed and built for engaging other battleships and were more expensive and less numerous compared to cruisers. Therefore, cruisers were often more widely used for escort duties due to their smaller size and greater flexibility.Why did battleships eventually become less popular compared to cruisers? Was it because of the rise of aerial warfare?Yes, the rise of aerial warfare played a significant role in the decline of battleships as a primary naval asset. The development of air power made battleships more vulnerable to attack, as they were large and slow-moving targets that were easily spotted from the air. Aircraft carriers and other smaller, more maneuverable ships, became more important in naval battles, as they were better equipped to handle the challenge of aerial warfare.

Additionally, advances in submarine technology made battleships vulnerable to underwater attacks. Submarines, which were smaller, faster and more difficult to detect, could launch torpedo attacks on battleships from a distance, causing significant damage or sinking the ships.

While battleships continued to serve in various naval engagements throughout the 20th century, they gradually became less important as their vulnerabilities became more pronounced. Today, battleships are no longer considered practical for modern naval warfare, and most have been decommissioned or turned into museum ships.So, are there any countries that still use battleships in their navy or are they completely obsolete now? The last operational battleships, the Iowa-class ships, were decommissioned by the United States Navy in the early 1990s. There are no countries that currently operate battleships as part of their naval fleet. 

However, a number of countries maintain historical ships as museum ships, including battleships. These ships are preserved and maintained as part of maritime history and are open to visitors to learn about the history of naval warfare. Some notable battleship museum ships include the USS Iowa in the United States, the HMS Belfast in the UK, and the Mikasa in Japan.If battleships are no longer practical, why does any country bother maintaining them as museum ships? First and foremost, they serve as tangible reminders of our naval history, and of the sacrifices and contributions made by sailors and others who served aboard them. These ships can provide insight into how naval warfare used to operate, including technology, tactics, and life at sea.

Secondly, museum ships can play an important role in educating the public, including students and tourists, about naval history and the importance of maritime power. By preserving these ships and allowing the public to visit them, museum ships offer a unique opportunity to learn about the past, and can inspire future generations to take an interest in history and naval history.

Finally, some countries see historical ships as an important part of their national heritage and pride, and maintaining them as museum ships is seen as an important cultural responsibility. While there are certainly costs associated with maintaining museum ships, many people feel that the benefits they provide to society more than outweigh these costs.But wouldn't it be more useful to allocate resources towards developing modern naval technology instead of preserving old ships that no longer have practical use? I don't see the point in spending money on maintaining something that can't be used for anything meaningful.It's true that developing modern naval technology is important, and that resources should be allocated towards it. However, preserving museum ships, including battleships, does not necessarily have to come at the expense of modernization efforts. In fact, many countries with museum ships are actively investing in modern naval technology.

Moreover, maintaining museum ships is often seen as an important cultural or educational responsibility, and is sometimes supported by private funding or other sources that do not compete directly with military budgets. Additionally, museum ships can serve as valuable training resources for sailors and naval personnel, providing them with hands-on experience with historical naval technology that can assist with their understanding of modern weapons platforms.

Ultimately, decisions about how to allocate resources among different priorities involve complex tradeoffs, and different countries may have different priorities that lead them to make different choices about preserving museum ships.I still think it's a waste of money to preserve old ships that can't be used for anything. However, there are also advantages to preserving museum ships that replicas and simulations cannot replicate. For one, museum ships offer an unparalleled opportunity to learn about and experience naval history in a tangible and immersive way. Visitors to museum ships can see and touch real historical artifacts, visit actual living quarters, and get a sense of what life at sea was like during different historical periods. These experiences can provide a unique and powerful educational experience that is difficult to replicate through simulations or replicas.

Additionally, museum ships can play an important role in historical research and preservation efforts. Researchers, historians, and other professionals can learn a great deal from studying actual historical ships, including the materials, construction techniques, and design innovations that were used in their creation.

Ultimately, different educational approaches will be appropriate for different circumstances, and there are benefits and challenges associated with each approach.

Write step-by-step instructions for making beef kebabs with clear and concise directions, including ingredients and measurements required. Additionally, include safety precautions for handling raw meat and using grilling equipment.Ingredients:
- 1 pound beef sirloin or tenderloin, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 1 large red onion, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 1 green bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
- 8-10 wooden skewers, soaked in water for at least 30 minutes
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 tablespoons red wine vinegar
- 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- Salt and black pepper to taste

Instructions:

1. In a mixing bowl, whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.

2. Add the cubed beef to the bowl and mix well, making sure each piece is coated with the marinade. Cover the bowl and allow to marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour or overnight.

3. Preheat the grill to medium heat.

4. Thread the marinated beef, onions, and peppers onto the soaked wooden skewers, alternating between beef and vegetables. Leave a small space at each end of the skewer for easy handling.

5. Place the skewers on the grill and cook for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until the beef is cooked to your desired doneness.

6. Remove the skewers from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes before serving.

Tips:

- To ensure that the beef kebabs are tender, use a tender cut of beef and marinate for at least 1 hour in the fridge.
- Soaking the wooden skewers in water prevents them from burning on the grill.
- You can add other vegetables to the skewers, such as mushrooms, zucchini, or cherry tomatoes.
- Be sure to wash your hands and utensils thoroughly after handling raw meat.

Instructions:

What impact does the location of oil reserves in the Middle East have on global politics and economics?The location of oil reserves in the Middle East has a significant impact on global politics and economics. Here are some of the impacts:

1. Dependence on oil: Many countries depend on oil imports from the Middle East to keep their economies running. This dependence gives the Middle Eastern countries significant political leverage over these countries.

2. Price fluctuations: Any changes in the availability or price of oil from the Middle East can have a ripple effect on the global economy. For example, an increase in the price of oil can lead to inflation, which can hurt the economies of many countries.

3. Geopolitics: The Middle East is a region that's always been of strategic importance, given the oil resources. As such, there has often been competition for influence in the region, which has led to many geopolitical conflicts.

4. Risk to supply chain: The Middle East is located in an unstable region, where conflict and political unrest are common. This instability makes the oil supply chain from the Middle East vulnerable to disruption. 

5. Resource curse: The presence of abundant resources like oil can often lead to a "resource curse," where the country becomes overly dependent on the resource and starts to neglect other sectors of the economy, leading to social and economic problems. 

Overall, the location of oil reserves in the Middle East has a profound impact on global politics and economics. Can I collaborate with others on a Pages document?Yes, you can collaborate with others on a Pages document by sharing the document with them and allowing them to edit it. You can also see the changes the collaborators make in real-time.That sounds great! Can I restrict certain collaborators from making changes to certain parts of the document?Yes, you can restrict certain collaborators from making changes to certain parts of the Pages document by using the "Restrict Editing" feature. Here's how to do it:

1. Open the Pages document that you want to share with others.
2. Click on the "Collaborate" button in the top-right corner of the screen.
3. In the Collaborate sidebar that appears on the right side of the screen, click on the "Share Options" button.
4. In the Share Options dialog box, select "Restrict Editing" from the permissions drop-down menu.
5. Click on the "+" button to add collaborators who can make unrestricted edits to the document.
6. Click on the "Edit" button next to each collaborator's name to edit their permissions.
7. In the "Add Restrictions" section of the Edit Collaborator dialog box, select the parts of the document that you want to restrict from being edited.
8. Click on the "Done" button to save your changes.

Once you've set up the restrictions, any collaborator who tries to edit the restricted parts of the document will be prompted to request permission to make the changes. You can then choose to approve or reject their request.Can I revoke editing access from a collaborator if I change my mind later on?Yes, you can revoke editing access from a collaborator if you change your mind later on. Here's how to do it:

1. Open the Pages document that you are sharing with others.
2. Click on the "Collaborate" button in the top-right corner of the screen.
3. In the Collaborate sidebar, click on the "Share Options" button.
4. In the Share Options dialog box, find the collaborator that you want to revoke access from and click on the "Edit" button next to their name.
5. In the Edit Collaborator dialog box, click on the "Revoke Access" button.
6. Confirm that you want to revoke the collaborator's access by clicking on the "Revoke Access" button again in the confirmation dialog box.

Once you have revoked access from a collaborator, they will no longer be able to view or edit the Pages document. You can also re-add them later on if you change your mind again.Wow, that's really helpful! It's great to know that Pages has so many collaboration features.You're very welcome! When designing for mobile devices you’ll generally want to plan specifically for mobile delivery rather than re-purpose an entire online course.
This is partly due to the size limitation of the mobile viewing area but also due to the nature of a mobile device. People typically use these devices on-the-go, grabbing a moment or two to check information or viewing mobile content while doing something else.
Consider what learning content is best for mLearning. Mobile devices are ideal for just-in-time, just-in-place learning. Supplemental material, field guides, how-to references, key learning points, and on-the-spot reminders are all great uses for mLearning.
For optimal viewing, try to keep important content within the screen viewing area. Users of mobile devices are more used to scrolling in order to see all of the content on their mobile. Claro doesn’t restrict the bottom of the mobile stage area, so you can create content that scrolls. You may want to add a visual marker such as a line or logo to denote the bottom of the page.
Ensure each topic (Learning Object) can be taken in a very short time. Consider the fact that Claro’s mobile player gives the learner easy access to jump directly to each topic, so breaking subjects into small topics makes sense.
Keep related information (e.g., items to compare or contrast) on one page but otherwise, as much as possible, break up information across pages to reduce scrolling.
Steer clear of non-standard fonts or you may run into odd spacing and line wrapping problems.Keep your font sizes legible as well; not too small but not too large either.
Course completion and test results are stored for future tracking. Claro’s mobile courses can be published as SCORM to an LMS or delivered and tracked directly from Claro.
Avoid adding Flash (.swf) files as these will not play on all mobile devices (e.g., on the iPhone and iPad).
Add interactivity to your courses using the tools in Claro, such as Actions, the Image Map, and Hotspots.
Any buttons or other interactive objects or links you make should be large enough to select by tapping with a finger (Apple suggests a minimum of 44x30 pixels for iOS devices).
Don't use "onMouseOver" events since these are not supported by mobile devices.
Don't use "onDblClick" events since these are used by mobile devices for zooming.
Use "onClick" events for mobile interactions. The click is a tap on a mobile. Make sure you refer to "tap" in your user directions. If your course is intended for mobile OR standard delivery, enter "Click or tap..." in your user directions.
Save your audio files as .mp3.
Save your video files as .mp4 h264. H.264 is an MPEG-4 compression standard for video. It delivers top video quality at about half the file size of MPEG-2.
Check your progress early and often by previewing your course in Claro using the simulator and also by checking it on the target mobile devices.
See Previewing a mobile course for more information.
Consider where you might add interactive Player Controls that prompt the learner to tap to answer or identify something. A correct tap moves the learner ahead without needing to tap the next button as well.
See Which mobile operating systems can Claro courses display on? for more information.
When designing specifically for the Apple iPad and iPhone in mind, consider Apple’s device considerations. In addition to avoiding adding Flash (swf or flv files), see our articles Audio cannot AutoPlay, Designing mobile courses with audio narration, and Do not embed From URL web objects.
Claro’s content doesn’t rely on Flash so it can be viewed on any mobile device. Claro output is HTML5. For more information, see Leveraging HTML5 to take your e-learning (and m-learning) into the future.

Can you explain the concept of threat intelligence and how it is used to identify potential cyber threats?Threat intelligence involves collecting, analyzing, and sharing information on potential cyber threats related to an organization. It encompasses a range of data sources such as open-source intelligence, community forums, and commercial feeds.

The information collected from these sources is used by organizations to identify potential cyber threats like malware, phishing scams, ransomware, and others that could have an impact on their system security. Based on this, security teams can develop security measures or countermeasures to prevent or mitigate the risk of attacks.

Threat intelligence provides up-to-date information on the latest methods used by attackers, their targets, and their motives. This information helps organizations to better understand their vulnerabilities, anticipate potential attacks, and take precautionary measures to prevent or minimize the impact of an attack.

Write a fictional short story, between 500-1000 words, with a protagonist who travels back in time. The story should have a clear and engaging plot, with rising action, a climax, and a satisfying resolution. Additionally, consider how the use of descriptive language and character development can enhance the reader's immersion in the story.Sarah had always been fascinated by the history of her country. She wanted to see the events that shaped her land and people firsthand. Although she had read many books and visited countless museums, it was never enough. She yearned to experience it all. So, when she heard a rumour about a time-travel device, she jumped at the chance of using it. Without a moment's hesitation, she entered the time machine and travelled back three centuries.

She stood outside the machine, wondering if it worked. Had she really travelled back in time? Maybe it was all a dream; she pinched herself to check. It was real. Sarah looked around, and the scenery was drastically different. The buildings were flat-roofed and made of mud and bricks. The streets were narrow and chaotic, and the people were dressed in colourful and elaborate clothes.

Sarah was standing in the middle of the town square. The merchants were busy selling their goods on the bustling street. Children were playing tag and running around. The sound of some lively music was coming from the nearby alleyway, where a group of musicians was performing. The smell of baking bread and cooking meat filled the air.

Sarah was spellbound, staring at the scene before her. It was like entering another world. She wanted to experience everything, talk to locals and learn about their lives. But, she had to be careful, she didn't want to cause a fuss, or worse, get caught. Sarah took the necessary precautions and adjusted her attire and language to match the era so she could blend in around the town.

She wandered around the town, observing the people and the architecture. She was fascinated by the way of life, the traditions and customs of the people. She had read about all of these in history books, but here, it was different. Then she noticed a group of men organising a protest against the high taxes imposed on the people by the British. She instantly knew that this was the Boston Tea Party. Sarah joined them and participated in the protest. It was electrifying to be a part of something so critical to the nation’s history. For the first time, Sarah felt brave and empowered.

After the protest, Sarah met several famous historical figures, which was awe-inspiring. The stars of the American Revolution were alive in front of her; George Washington, Benjamin Franklin and John Adams, among others. It was like she was living in one of her favourite historical books.

However, Sarah had been anxious about meddling with history or doing something that might cause trouble. But, the thrill of being a part of it all was tempting. Please provide a recipe for a salad or wrap that includes lean protein, leafy greens, and healthy fats to keep you energized and alert for the entire day. Additionally, please ensure that the recipe is easy to prepare, portable, and can be customized to fit any dietary restrictions.Chicken and Avocado Salad

Ingredients:
- 2 cups of mixed leafy greens (spinach, lettuce, arugula)
- 1 medium chicken breast (grilled and sliced)
- 1/2 avocado (diced)
- 1/4 cup of cherry tomatoes (halved)
- 1/4 cup of cucumber slices
- 2 tablespoons of chopped almonds
- 2 tablespoons of dried cranberries
- 1 tablespoon of olive oil
- 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:

1. Start by grilling the chicken breast until fully cooked. Let it cool and slice into thin pieces.
2. In a large bowl, mix the greens, chicken, avocado, cherry tomatoes, and cucumber.
3. Add the chopped almonds and dried cranberries to the bowl and mix well.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper. Pour it over the salad and toss to coat evenly.
5. Serve the salad immediately or store it in a portable container for later.

This recipe can be customized to fit any dietary restriction by replacing the chicken with tofu, grilled shrimp, or salmon. The nuts and dried fruit can also be substituted for sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, or raisins.This recipe looks great, but can you suggest some other dressing options that would complement the flavors in the salad? Spicy Lime Dressing

Ingredients:
• 2 tablespoons of lime juice
• 1 tablespoon of honey or maple syrup
• 1 teaspoon of sriracha hot sauce
• 1 clove of garlic, minced
• 2 tablespoons of olive oil
• Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:
1. In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, honey or maple syrup, sriracha, and garlic.
2. Slowly whisk in the olive oil until the dressing is emulsified and well combined.
3. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
4. Drizzle the dressing over the chicken and avocado salad.

Analyze the use of renewable energy in waste management and resource recovery.Renewable energy is becoming increasingly important in waste management and resource recovery. The use of renewable energy in these industries can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions, conserve resources, and reduce dependence on non-renewable energy sources. There are several ways in which renewable energy is being used in waste management and resource recovery.

Landfill Gas Energy Recovery: One of the most common ways renewable energy is being used in waste management is by capturing and utilizing landfill gas. Landfill gas is a mixture of methane, carbon dioxide, and other gases that are produced by the decomposition of organic waste. The gas can be captured using wells and then burned to generate electricity or heat. Approximately 648 landfill gas energy projects are operating in the United States, with a total capacity of 2,430 megawatts.

Anaerobic Digestion: Another way renewable energy is being used in waste management is through anaerobic digestion. Anaerobic digestion is a process that breaks down organic waste in the absence of oxygen, producing biogas and a nutrient-rich fertilizer. Biogas can be burned to generate electricity, while the fertilizer can be used to improve soil health. Anaerobic digestion is used in a variety of settings, including wastewater treatment plants, farms, and industrial facilities.

Waste-to-Energy: Waste-to-energy is another way renewable energy is being used in waste management. Waste-to-energy involves burning waste to generate electricity, typically in specialized facilities called waste-to-energy plants. The process can reduce the volume of waste that ends up in landfills and can generate electricity from waste that might otherwise be difficult to dispose of. Some waste-to-energy plants also use the heat generated by the burning process to provide district heating.

Conclusion: The use of renewable energy in waste management and resource recovery is becoming more common and important. Landfill gas energy recovery, anaerobic digestion, and waste-to-energy all provide ways to generate electricity from waste while reducing greenhouse gas emissions and conserving resources. As renewable energy technology continues to improve, we can expect to see even more innovative ways to integrate renewable energy into waste management and resource recovery.Can you add some details about the potential economic benefits of using renewable energy in this industry?Certainly! There are various potential economic benefits of using renewable energy in waste management and resource recovery. Here are some of them:

1. Cost savings: Utilizing renewable energy sources like landfill gas, anaerobic digestion, and waste-to-energy can significantly reduce operational costs in waste management and resource recovery. With renewable energy, these industries can generate their own electricity, which means lower energy bills and the ability to sell excess energy back to the grid. 2. Revenue generation: Waste management companies can generate revenue by selling carbon credits due to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, the sale of electricity generated from renewable energy sources and biogas can create additional revenue streams. 3. Job creation: The development and operation of renewable energy facilities create jobs, both in the construction and maintenance of the plants. 4. Reduced dependence on non-renewable energy sources: The use of renewable energy in waste management can reduce dependence on non-renewable energy sources like fossil fuels, which can be vulnerable to price fluctuations or supply disruptions. 5. Improved waste management efficiency: Using renewable energy sources that also result in waste reduction, such as anaerobic digestion, can improve overall waste management efficiency, reducing costs related to transportation, storage, and disposal. Here are some tips for effectively using evidence to support arguments in an analytical essay:

1. Choose reputable sources: When selecting evidence to support your arguments, make sure you are using reliable and credible sources. This will help strengthen your argument and lend it more credibility.

2. Use a variety of evidence: Diversify your sources to strengthen your argument. This includes using academic journals, books, reputable news sources, and expert opinions.

3. Provide context: When introducing evidence, provide context that explains why it is relevant to your argument. This will help readers understand the significance of the evidence and how it supports your argument.

4. Analyze the evidence: Don't just present the evidence; analyze it! Explain how and why the evidence supports your argument. Be sure to connect the evidence back to your thesis statement.

5. Use quotes and paraphrasing: When using evidence, be sure to properly cite your sources. You can quote directly from your sources, or paraphrase the ideas in your own words. Just make sure you are accurately representing the original source.

Here is a piece of text: The peer economy has risks for participants, but a little more sharing could make it a lot better.
Companies like Airbnb, RelayRides, Lyft, Sidecar, Amazon Mechanical Turk, and TaskRabbit are all platforms where anyone can become an entrepreneur, renting out their cars, their homes, or simply their time to the highest bidder. In Silicon Valley, this move is cast as a disruptive unleashing of untapped value, and an empowering opportunity for participants.
There’s another way of looking at these participatory platforms, though, and that’s through a murky lens of exploitation. Let’s stipulate that the traditional economy isn’t exactly protecting the quality of jobs–unless you’re excited about working as a “human robot” in an Amazon fulfillment center. Still, in the traditional economy, as in bowling, there are rules. Whether you’re a hotel maid, a cab driver, a delivery person for UPS, a software tester or graphic designer, you’re entitled to a minimum wage, worker protections, and maybe some basic benefits.
Is Airbnb Actually Good for New York?
Does the Sharing Economy Have a Shadow Side?
However, if you do the equivalent of the same work on one of these newfangled participatory platforms–rent out a room in your home on Airbnb, give rides to strangers in your car via Sidecar, make runs to IKEA for Taskrabbit, design logos on 99Designs, or complete tiny tasks on Fiverr or Mechanical Turk–you’re not entitled to any of the above. Estimates of average earnings on Mechanical Turk range from $1.20-$5 an hour.
Recent news, however, suggests that the same technology that created the participatory economy could also make it more fair. Turkopticon is a browser plugin co-created by an ex-Googler that grafts a reputation system onto Amazon Mechanical Turk. It lets Mechanical Turks see reviews of employers (aka “requesters”) that are written by their peers, and avoid scammers or those who don’t pay. The cofounder, Lilly Irani, calls it “a tool to spark awareness” of the broader labor issues facing people whose gigs have become microgigs.
In other words, if the next TaskRabbit or Mechanical Turk were owned and run by the Rabbits and the Turks, they’d be truly people-powered, and truly disruptive.

It would ensure that workers are entitled to minimum wage, worker protections, and basic benefits, which they are not currently receiving. Additionally, it may spark awareness of broader labor issues facing people whose gigs have become microgigs. Here are a few more examples of participatory platforms and some risks they may pose for workers:

- Uber/Lyft: Drivers who work for these ride-hailing platforms are considered independent contractors, meaning they don't receive benefits or minimum wage protections. Additionally, drivers bear the cost of maintaining their own cars, and Uber and Lyft can cut their rates without much notice, potentially leading to lower earnings for drivers.
- Instacart/Shipt: These platforms allow people to order groceries online and have them delivered by a personal shopper. The shoppers, however, are often considered independent contractors and don't receive benefits or minimum wage protections. According to a recent report, some shoppers have reported making as little as $7 per hour.
- Upwork/Freelancer: These platforms allow companies to hire freelancers for a variety of tasks, from software development to writing to design work. However, since the work is often done remotely, freelancers may not have the protections they would in a traditional office setting. Additionally, since freelancers are competing against each other for work, there may be a race to the bottom in terms of rates and compensation.

Overall, while these participatory platforms can offer opportunities for people to make money, they also come with risks for workers, who may not be protected under traditional labor laws.Can you explain how the peer economy is viewed by some as exploitative?Sure! Some people view the peer economy, or the sharing economy, as exploitative because it often relies on independent contractors who don't receive the same protections and benefits as traditional employees. For example, someone who rents out a room on Airbnb or drives for Uber is not considered an employee of the company and is therefore not entitled to minimum wage or worker protections such as health insurance, vacation time, or sick leave. 

Additionally, some critics argue that the uneven power dynamic between the platform owners and the workers on the platform can lead to exploitation. For example, if workers have few options to find work outside of a particular platform or if they're competing against each other for work, they may be forced to accept low pay or work long hours. 

Finally, some people argue that the peer economy can contribute to the erosion of traditional jobs and industries, leading to job insecurity for many workers. For example, the rise of Airbnb has led to concerns about its impact on the hotel industry and its workers. 

Of course, not everyone agrees with these critiques of the peer economy, and there are certainly benefits to participating in these platforms as well. But overall, some people see it as a system that can be exploitative of workers.

Assess the ways in which grunge music challenged mainstream rock norms and attitudes and explore the lasting cultural significance of the genre in music and society today.Grunge music, also known as the Seattle sound, emerged in the early 1990s in Seattle, Washington. It was a subgenre of alternative rock, and was characterized by its heavy guitar riffs, angst-filled lyrics and raw sound.

The origins of grunge music can be traced back to the 1980s punk and hardcore scenes in Seattle, which were influenced by bands like Black Flag, the Sex Pistols and the Stooges. These scenes were centered around small clubs and DIY venues like the Metropolis and the Gorilla Room.

One of the earliest grunge bands was Green River, which formed in 1984 and featured future members of Pearl Jam and Mudhoney. Other prominent grunge bands that emerged in the late 1980s and early 1990s included Soundgarden, Alice in Chains, Mudhoney, and Nirvana.

Nirvana, led by Kurt Cobain, became the face of the grunge movement, and their second album, "Nevermind," released in 1991, became a massive commercial success, selling millions of copies worldwide. The album's lead single, "Smells Like Teen Spirit," became an anthem for disaffected youth and propelled grunge music and culture into the mainstream.

Grunge music challenged mainstream rock norms and attitudes, which were often characterized by flashy costumes, polished studio recordings, and virtuosic musicianship. Grunge, on the other hand, emphasized authenticity, simplicity and a "do-it-yourself" ethos, which was embraced by many young people who were disillusioned with the excesses of mainstream culture.

In terms of style, grunge was characterized by a relatively simple and stripped-down sound, with heavy guitars and simple drum patterns. Many grunge bands incorporated elements of punk rock, heavy metal, and hard rock into their sound, creating a unique blend of musical styles.

The cultural impact of grunge music can still be felt today. Many of the major grunge bands of the 1990s continue to be celebrated and remembered as pioneers of alternative rock. The style and attitude of grunge also continues to be an influential force in contemporary popular culture, with many young musicians and fans continuing to embrace the DIY ethos and independent spirit of the movement.

In conclusion, grunge music emerged as a unique and powerful cultural force in the early 1990s, challenging mainstream rock norms and attitudes with its raw sound, angst-filled lyrics and DIY ethos. Explain the chronological steps of the water cycle, including the changes in water state and the location of each process, and analyze how the water cycle influences weather patterns on a global scale. Use scientific jargon and provide specific examples to support your argument.The water cycle, also known as the hydrological cycle, is a continuous process that involves the movement of water between the atmosphere, land, and oceans. The water cycle consists of several steps or processes that occur in a chronological order. These include evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, runoff, and transpiration.

The first step in the water cycle is evaporation. During this process, water from oceans, lakes, rivers, plants or soil surfaces is heated by the sun, which causes the water molecules to break free from the surface tension and become water vapor. This water vapor rises up into the atmosphere and forms clouds.

The second step is condensation. As water vapor rises into the atmosphere, it cools and condenses into tiny water droplets or ice crystals, which form clouds. The process of condensation releases heat into the atmosphere, providing energy for the formation of storms and atmospheric disturbances.

The third step is precipitation. When the cloud droplets become too heavy, they fall back to the earth as precipitation in the form of rain, snow, sleet, or hail. Precipitation can occur anywhere on Earth, but it is most common in areas with high humidity and high levels of atmospheric moisture.

The fourth step is infiltration. When precipitation falls on land, it can either run off into nearby bodies of water or infiltrate the soil. Infiltration is the process by which water seeps into the ground through the soil and becomes groundwater. This water may eventually make its way to aquifers, which are underground layers of rock that hold water.

The fifth step is runoff. When precipitation falls on land and does not infiltrate the soil, it runs off into nearby bodies of water, such as rivers, lakes, and oceans. Runoff can also occur when the ground is saturated, and the inﬁltrated water cannot be absorbed.

The sixth and final step is transpiration. This is the process by which plants absorb water through their roots and then release it into the atmosphere through their leaves. Transpiration contributes to the moisture in the atmosphere and helps plants to cool down.

The water cycle plays an important role in influencing weather patterns on a global scale. The process of evaporation from oceans and other bodies of water releases moisture into the atmosphere, which can influence the formation of clouds and precipitation. Precipitation can lead to flooding, landslides, and other natural disasters that can affect weather patterns. The water cycle also helps to regulate the Earth's temperature, as the process of evaporation and condensation releases and absorbs heat in the atmosphere. This, in turn, can affect the formation of weather patterns such as hurricanes and typhoons.

Overall, the water cycle is a vital process for the world's ecosystem and climate. It plays an essential role in maintaining the balance of water resources on the planet and influences weather patterns on a global scale.That was a great explanation of the water cycle! Could you include some more specific examples of how the water cycle influences weather patterns? Also, can you explain how climate change is affecting the water cycle and weather patterns globally?Sure! Here are some specific examples of how the water cycle influences weather patterns:

- The water cycle helps to fuel thunderstorms and hurricanes by providing the large amounts of moisture needed for these storms to form and intensify. The process of evaporation from the warm ocean surface helps to provide the necessary moisture for these storms.

- Heavy rainfall and flooding can occur when there is a disruption in the water cycle, causing more precipitation than the land can absorb or carry away. For example, if an area experiences prolonged heavy rainfall, the soil may become saturated, leading to increased runoff and flooding.

- Drought can occur in regions where there is a lack of precipitation or prolonged periods of dry weather. This often happens when the water cycle is disrupted, and evaporation and transpiration exceed precipitation, leading to a decrease in available water resources.

Climate change is having a significant impact on the water cycle and weather patterns globally. Rising temperatures due to climate change are causing an increase in the rate of evaporation from oceans, lakes, and other bodies of water, which can lead to more frequent and severe storms. This increased evaporation also contributes to a decrease in available water resources in some areas, which can lead to drought and other issues.

Climate change is also causing changes in precipitation patterns, with some areas receiving more precipitation than usual, while other areas experience prolonged droughts. These changes can impact agriculture, water availability, and other aspects of human life.

In addition to these impacts, climate change is also causing the melting of glaciers and ice caps, which contributes to sea level rise and further changes in weather patterns. Overall, the water cycle is strongly linked to climate change, and understanding these connections is crucial for addressing the impacts of climate change on the environment and human society.That was really informative! Climate change affects the water cycle in a variety of ways, and these changes, in turn, can have significant impacts on local weather patterns in different regions.

One of the most significant impacts of climate change on the water cycle is an overall increase in evaporation rates due to higher temperatures. This increased evaporation rate leads to an increase in moisture in the atmosphere, which can contribute to more frequent and intense precipitation events, such as heavy rainstorms and snowstorms. For example, in the United States, the frequency of heavy precipitation events has increased by 30 percent since the early 1900s due to climate change.

However, in many regions, increased evaporation rates paired with higher temperatures can also lead to more frequent and severe droughts. Warming temperatures increase the demand for water, making it harder for areas that are already arid to support growing populations and agriculture. This has led to water shortages and increased the risk of wildfires in many areas, including parts of California and Australia.

Another impact of climate change on the water cycle is the melting of glaciers and polar ice caps. The melting of these ice masses contributes to a rise in sea levels, which can lead to flooding in coastal areas. In many coastal regions of the world, sea levels have already risen by about 8 inches since 1880 due to melting glaciers and ice caps.

The impact of climate change on the water cycle and local weather patterns is complex and non-uniform across different regions of the world. For instance, regions with a Mediterranean climate like California are expected to experience more frequent and intense droughts, whereas in tropical regions like Southeast Asia, heavier precipitation events are expected to increase the risk of flooding. Overall, the impact of climate change on the water cycle is a global issue and requires a coordinated response to mitigate its effects. Understanding these impacts is crucial for policymakers to develop adaptation strategies to protect communities from the adverse effects of climate change.

Here is a piece of text: Yes, our perception of old is a moving target, and it depends on … well, it depends on how many candles you’ve managed to collect on the birthday cake.
If you want proof that old age has become a flexible milestone, look no further than the 2017 U.S. Trust Insights on Wealth and Worth report that shows how four different generations view senior citizenship. Not surprisingly, the older you are, the longer it takes to achieve such status.
For the silent generation, those 73 or older, senior citizenship arrives at 73, the exact same age baby boomers also selected as the beginning of twilight. Millennials, the generation between 21 and 36 years old, clocked it at 59 and Generation X, the 37- to 52-year-olds, at 65. For me this is proof that old age, like beauty, is in the eye of the beholder.
The generations were similarly divided when it comes to pinpointing the end of youth. The silent generation puts it at 35 and boomers and Gen Xers at 31. Millennials, however, believe one stops being young at 40. Which may explain why this generation, often criticized (wrongly, I believe) for taking too long to grow up, has popularized the term “adulting,” the long and overwrought process of accomplishing certain markers (i.e., getting a job, moving out of your parents’ home, marriage and children) on the way to independence.
Sorting through old black-and-white photos I inherited from my mother, I found one of my paternal great-grandmother, a formidable woman whose limited education did little to dampen the fierce ambition she had for her children and grandchildren. In the photo she wears a black dress notable for its absolute lack of shape and charm. Gray hair bound in a net, she scowls at the camera.
I gauged her age at 80. But judging from the setting and the other people in the picture, my father said she was, more likely, in her early 60s. How then did she look so ancient? Then I remembered the advice my father gave me a few months ago, when I turned 60: “From now on every day is a gift. In your grandmother’s time, many didn’t even make it to this birthday.” It was an unusual comment from a person whose family is known for its longevity.
If 60 was accepted as old at the beginning of the 20th century, when babies born in 1900 had a life expectancy of 50, it certainly isn’t considered so anymore. Modern medicine has extended our life spans and we, in turn, have stretched the passages that mark the road from spring to winter.
Today, age truly is just a number. “Old” is no longer a facile label. While there’s no denying the inexorable march of time (dimming eyes and creaky joints being my least favorite), attitude may prove to be the elusive Fountain of Youth. A zest for life, an interest in the world, the pursuit of a passion, a desire to learn, a conscientious effort to keep mentally and physically healthy — those seem to be more telling qualities of true youth.
On those terms, I plan to remain a perpetual 32.

Pandora Media Inc. Experiences location based marketing flub.
Pandora, the online radio company, gives mobile advertisers the ability to target their users through the zip code the consumer enters upon signing up but, what has recently been discovered, is that the trouble with this mobile marketing technique is if the advertiser’s customers do not manually change their zip code data in the event that they move, they will continue to receive adds that would only be relevant to their previous place of address.
Many mobile ads that use latitude and longitude for targeting a user’s location are inaccurate.
According to a recent Thinknear survey of 53 million ad impressions, only 34% of mobile ads that use geolocation technology for the purpose of targeting mobile users in a specific location are accurate within 328 feet (100 meters). Meanwhile, 27% are inaccurate by over 32808 feet (10,000 meters).
Thinknear General Manager Eli Portnoy said that mobile users on the go create problems for these apps. Although an application developer may believe to have the proper longitude and latitude coordinates that are equal to a one meter (3.2 ft) by one meter location on a map, in reality, these coordinates could be way off by hundreds of meters. Therefore, if an app publisher utilized the zip code that was entered in during sign up as a central point, the user could, in fact, be traveling in a completely different zip code.
To boost its mobile marketing technique, Pandora has started to check IP addresses.
According to Pandora, the majority of its advertisers are interested in running large-scale campaigns that are nationwide. They have no interest in trying to reach mobile users who are located on a specific city block. For this reason, the internet radio company does not try for a target that would be narrower than zip code.
To enhance its more targeted advertisements, Pandora is now checking from where the IP address of a mobile device is coming and will notify a user to change their zip code if this is required. Pandora’s director of product management, Jack Krawczyk, said that the company’s surveys have revealed that its mobile marketing location accuracy scores are in the high 90s on a percentage scale due to the fact that people do not move that often.
Can you summarize the challenges with location-based advertising on mobile devices, as highlighted by the Thinknear survey?A recent survey by Thinknear has revealed challenges with location-based advertising on mobile devices. The use of geolocation technology for targeting mobile users in a specific location was found to be inaccurate, with only 34% of mobile ads accurate within 328 feet (100 meters) and 27% of ads inaccurate by over 32808 feet (10,000 meters). This is due to app developers using longitude and latitude coordinates that may be off by hundreds of meters and not accounting for users who may have moved and not updated their location data. To improve its location-based advertising, Pandora is now checking IP addresses to ensure accuracy.Can you find any other companies who have had similar issues with location-based marketing?Yes. McDonald's faced similar challenges with their mobile app's location-based marketing. In 2018, customers reported receiving push notifications and promotional deals for restaurants that were far away from their actual location. This was due to the app's use of inaccurate location data, resulting in frustrated customers and a negative experience. McDonald's had to work on improving the location accuracy of their app to prevent these issues from recurring.Interesting. Can you find any other examples of companies that have improved their location-based marketing accuracy in a similar way as Pandora?Yes. Yelp, a popular restaurant and business review platform, also improved its location-based marketing accuracy by checking the IP addresses of mobile devices. In 2020, Yelp added an automatic location detection feature to its app, which uses a user's IP address to determine their location instead of relying solely on their device's GPS. This has resulted in more accurate location-based results for users and more effective advertising for businesses on the platform. Other companies that have improved their location-based marketing accuracy include Foursquare, which uses a combination of GPS and Wi-Fi signals to pinpoint a user's location, and Facebook, which also uses IP addresses to supplement GPS data.That's interesting. Can you give me some tips on how to improve my location-based advertising accuracy for my own business?Yes, here are some tips to improve your location-based advertising accuracy for your own business:

1. Use multiple sources of location data: Relying solely on one source of location data, such as GPS, can lead to inaccurate targeting. Incorporating other sources of data, like Wi-Fi and IP addresses, can lead to more accurate results.

2. Regularly update location data: Encourage users to update their location data regularly, especially if they've moved or changed their address. You can also use push notifications or emails to remind users to update their location data.

3. Use Geo-fencing: Geo-fencing allows you to set a virtual boundary around a specific location, such as a store or event venue, and target users within that boundary. This can lead to more accurate targeting and higher engagement.

4. Test and analyze: Continuously monitor and analyze the performance of your location-based advertising campaigns to determine what's working and what's not. This will allow you to make adjustments and improve accuracy over time.

5. Be transparent: Be transparent with users about how you're using their location data and allow them to opt-out if they choose. This will help build trust with your audience and lead to more effective advertising in the long run.

But according to a watchdog appointed by Congress, those billions of dollars are at risk because the World Bank and the government of Afghanistan are not adequately monitoring where they go and how they are used.
"Once the U.S. Or any other donor provides its contributions to the fund, neither the World Bank nor USAID can account for how those funds are specifically spent," said the Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction in a statement. SIGAR is tasked with monitoring U.S. Spending in Afghanistan, and the U.S. Provides money to the fund through USAID.
The ARTF describes itself as the "the largest single source of on-budget financing for Afghanistan's development ... Delivering important results within key sectors including education, health, agriculture, rural development, infrastructure, and governance." It does not fund Afghanistan's security sector.
The funds from the trust fund are used to pay salaries of Afghan government workers, SIGAR says, but the World Bank does not require a third-party monitor to physically verify that those government workers actually exist.
The third party contractor's work is limited by security concerns because they are not always able to verify workers in insecure areas, the report states. The World Bank also does not publicly share evaluations of the third-party contractors who are monitoring how the money is used.
"Donors, including USAID and U.S. Taxpayers, will continue to provide billions of dollars to the ARTF without adequate assurance that the money being spent is actually contributing to the ongoing operation of the Afghan government, addressing fiscal gaps in Afghanistan's national budget, and furthering the international community's overall reconstruction efforts," the report states.
The World Bank also is not consistently measuring performance of projects funded by the ARTF, according to the watchdog. "Without an accurate, reliable evaluation, the World Bank will be unable to determine the impact the roughly $10 billion in donor funding has had in improving Afghan development."
The fact that there is apparently little accountability for how the money is spent has an impact on the projects selected, according to the report: "A senior aide to Afghanistan's President told us that the structure of the ARTF allows for ill-conceived projects to be funded because there is no repayment obligation and that dysfunctional projects are nearly impossible to eliminate."
There's political pressure to spend the money, the aide reportedly said, "even if the programs and projects being funded are ill-conceived or unneeded, or risk losing future funding."
The World Bank responded to the report by saying that most of its findings "are somewhat anecdotal, and do not fully take into account measures taken to improve the reporting on how funds are used."
"Independent assessments conclude that in Afghanistan's volatile context, the ARTF is a vehicle of choice for pooled on-budget funding given its low transaction and management costs, transparency and accountability," the World Bank said in a statement. "It provides a well-functioning arena for policy debate and consensus creation between the international community and government of Afghanistan while delivering important results to millions of Afghans across the country."

SYDNEY, N.S. — The Nova Scotia Health Authority has named the staff members who are leading the functional planning process for the redevelopment of the health-care system in the Cape Breton Regional Municipality.
In an email to the Cape Breton Post, Kristen Lipscombe, a spokesperson for the NSHA, wrote that Mark LeCouter is serving as the team’s senior director. He is a registered nurse and was previously zone director for critical care services, regional medicine, cardiac and respiratory services.
Mickey Daye, also a registered nurse, is the clinical director responsible for the redevelopment work covering New Waterford and North Sydney. He was the director of integrated health for hospitals in Glace Bay, New Waterford and North Sydney and the site lead for Northside General Hospital.
Another registered nurse, Troy Penney, is the director responsible for the expansions at the Glace Bay and Cape Breton regional hospitals. He was previously zone director of perioperative services and pain services.
The positions were posted and filled this fall. Other team members are expected to be added as the process progresses, including physician and clinical and support services leaders.
In June, the Stephen McNeil Liberal government and the NSHA announced the redevelopment of the region’s health-care system including expansions of the Cape Breton Cancer Centre and emergency departments at the Cape Breton Regional and Glace Bay hospitals, and the closure of hospitals in New Waterford and North Sydney, which are to be replaced with health centres without emergency departments.
At the time, officials said that a nine- to 12-month functional planning process would be undertaken to determine more details about what the renovated and new facilities would look like. That process is to examine items such as the amount of space needed, project patient needs and the scope and role of services that are part of the expansions and community health centres.
When asked for an update on where things currently stand in that process, Lipscombe said the process began in the summer and is still expected to take nine to 12 months.
The Cape Breton Post obtained under Freedom of Information a series of assessments performed on the existing buildings dating as far back as 2013 and published a series of stories on their current conditions. One of the stories looked at findings of a draft facility review summary report prepared for the Department of Transportation and Infrastructure Renewal and the NSHA-based on site visits between March 5-7 of this year. John Malcom, retired CEO of the former Cape Breton District Health Authority, said after reading it there appears to be much more work to do.
“There’s nothing wrong with what they did, they did what I would call a visual inspection, a walk-around, it’s not in-depth, so I would hope that as they go forward they’re going to have to do much more in-depth,” Malcom said.
One concern that Malcom has relates to the Northside General, which he describes as really being two buildings, with a major addition built in the late 1980s that he said is in good condition.
“The older part of the building where the patients are housed is probably the oldest hospital building still holding patients (in the area), but there’s a newer part and I’m just surprised they’re walking away from that,” he said.
Malcom — who stressed that while he worked in health-care administration in Cape Breton for 16 years, he has now been retired for a half-dozen — also expressed some skepticism about the timing of when construction may actually proceed, noting a redevelopment of the Victoria General in Halifax is also underway.
